summary: Suwon Airport (SWU/RKSW) is a military airfield primarily operated by the Republic of Korea Air Force, located just south of central Suwon in Gyeonggi Province. While it has historically supported limited civilian charter operations, it functions mainly as a military installation rather than a commercial passenger hub. Travelers using this facility should coordinate access through official channels due to its restricted nature.
faqs:
Q: Does Suwon Airport handle regular commercial passenger flights?
A: No, Suwon Airport operates primarily as a Republic of Korea Air Force base. Civilian commercial service is not regularly scheduled, and access is generally restricted.

Q: Which commercial airport is closest to Suwon for travelers?
A: Gimpo International Airport (GMP) in Seoul and Incheon International Airport (ICN) are the most convenient alternatives, both reachable within roughly one to two hours by road or rail.

Q: Is Suwon Airport open to the general public?
A: Access is limited due to its military role. Visitors without official authorization should not expect to enter the facility freely.

Q: What is Suwon best known for?
A: Suwon is famous for Hwaseong Fortress, an 18th-century UNESCO World Heritage Site, as well as its role as a major technology and manufacturing hub.
transport_tips: Reaching Suwon Airport is easiest by car or taxi, with the facility a short drive south of Suwon city center and about 30 km south of Seoul. From Suwon Station, taxis typically take 15–20 minutes depending on traffic. The Suin-Bundang Line and Line 1 of the Seoul Metro serve Suwon but do not stop at the airport itself.
local_tip: If visiting the Suwon area, plan time to walk the Hwaseong Fortress walls at sunset—the lighting and elevated views over the old city make it one of Korea's most photogenic heritage sites, and it's only a short ride from the airport.
